question.problem:
Suppose that the function $f(x,y)$ and all of its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U.$ Find the values of $a$ and $b$, if 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =a{y}^{3}{e}^{x-1}+3{x}^{2}{e}^{y-1}, \\ {f}_{y}(x,y) & ={x}^{3}{e}^{y-1}+3b{y}^{2}{e}^{x-1}, \\ {f}_{x}(1,1) & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the mixed partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(a{y}^{3}{e}^{x-1}+3{x}^{2}{e}^{y-1}) \\  & =3a{y}^{2}{e}^{x-1}+3{x}^{2}{e}^{y-1} \\ {f}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}{e}^{y-1}+3b{y}^{2}{e}^{x-1}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}{e}^{y-1}+3b{y}^{2}{e}^{x-1}\end{aligned}
$$

Since the function and its first and second-order partial derivatives are continuous on an open set $U,$ the mixed partial derivatives must be equal. Hence, we have the identity

$$
\begin{aligned}3a{y}^{2}{e}^{x-1}+3{x}^{2}{e}^{y-1}=3{x}^{2}{e}^{y-1}+3b{y}^{2}{e}^{x-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients of ${y}^{2}{e}^{x-1},$ respectively, we see that $a=b.$ 

Since ${f}_{x}(1,1)=4$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,1) & =4 \\ a(1)^{3}{e}^{0}+3(1)^{2}{e}^{0} & =4 \\ a+3 & =4 \\ a & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
b=a=1.
$$
